# Chapter Five: Nero

> *"Your parents are the monument to your past, do not dishonor them."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

“Let us give thanks and honor our emissary” Muric Nero stated from the small podium at the front of the congregation, the tiny collection of worshipers bowed their heads in reverence as they sat lined up along the dark wooden pews, he heard the whispered thanks from the group of townsfolk as he stood there smiling, studying his flock as a parent would a child.

Muric was a young man, only indoctrinated this past year into the Messengers unfortunately the old Messenger Loprin Birin had died unexpectedly giving Muric the job long before he would have been ascended to full Messenger, it had been a hard transition the Messenger reflected, but one he had settled into nicely.

Muric was proud of his role, his boyish good looks and earnest face made him easy to talk to by the townspeople and they had accepted him quickly, which was rare in the small towns of Vicor.

He had settled into the job with a caring efficiency and enthusiasm. Muric had come to be a Messenger in the same way a lot of young men of means did.

He was the second son of a lord and in order to ensure that Muric would not threaten the line of succession he was given to the church.

Forced to denounce his title and wealth he was no longer the son of lord, just a simple Messenger here to deliver the word of Aurtus to those who needed it. He had never liked the life he had led prior to the church, looking out over the simple townspeople his smile widening My people he thought correcting himself.

His father had been an abusive drunk, and his brother sought to ensure Muric knew who was in charge by way of beatings and humiliation.

Entering the old Stone monastery was frightening as a young boy but quickly he had found a home among the old monks who were pleasant and treated him with kindness, he was taught the history of the world and shown how to help those less fortunate, they taught him nobility and self-sacrifice, lessons he took to heart and they soon became integral to his person.

This was truly his calling he reflected as the congregation rose their heads expectantly, hope in the faces of those along the pews.

Muric nodded and said the final blessing in the well-practiced tone of one who had done it often “Go forth, honor others as you wish to be honored, know that today is a special day for you are loved by Aurtus”.

With that the congregation rose “Praise be to Aurtus” they rang out the words vibrating off of the old rafters as the group began to shuffle down the pew’s and onto the burgundy runner, they slowly made their way in a line out into the morning sun.

Muric followed the group into the morning light taking a position to the left of the door he made small talk and greeted every parishioner, talking and shaking hands with his congregation as they asked questions and made appointments for later in the week.

The Messenger of a town was more than just the pathway to the gods, he was the mayor, the first line of law, the judge and the clerk if he couldn’t solve it then it would go before the lord seer, that alone usually meant he solved most issues, for no one wanted to chance the wrath of the Lord.

He was also a counselor and friend to all and that made Muric happy, his life was full of children, his children. Though they were older than he, Nero was proud of them and their accomplishments and grieved and commiserated with them as if they were his own family. The thought always made him happy. Complete, even.

The middle Burik boy approached his gate slow as he came to stand in front of Nero, his head down as he waited for the Messenger to speak, last week he had been caught stealing from the farm next door and his punishment had been a free week of labor to the family who owned it.

“Master Burik, how goes your labors?” Nero asked with a mock reproving tone, the young man stood there in the simple cotton dress of a farmer as he shuffled his feet doing his best not to meet Nero’s eyes, after a moment he spoke, his tone soft “Fine, today is my final day Messenger” he stated and Nero nodded in approval.

“Let’s hope this is the last time young man, next time the punishment will be more severe,” he finished.

A smile spreading across his face when he was done “Now, go it is time for the feast,” he said and the boy’s head came up as a smile spread across his dirty cheeks, what young man could turn down free food he thought to himself as the kid enthusiastically nodded and tore across the center of town.

Muric waved as the people moved off towards the main hall where the volunteers had begun to lay out the dishes and baste the smoked pig, the celebration was one of accomplishment and friendship, allowing the community to come together and share the bounty of the village.

Muric raised his face to the sky and closed his eyes as he breathed in the cold morning air. Winter was on its way he thought and soon people would shelter in and the mass would thin out as snow came to the land.

Walking back towards the keep he caught the snippet of a conversation and steered himself towards the voices. Muric could hear the low voices as they argued amongst themselves.

“Good morning gentlemen how are you this fine Son morning” he said, and they nodded and smiled at the Messenger. He listened as the men talked about the trail of fire a few nights prior “It’s a sign from above, Aurtus is angry,” said Korl. The man was a simple farmer but always willing to attribute anything as a sign that the gods were angry with man.

He had more than one conversation with the man regarding this and Muric did his best to avoid rolling his eyes at the old farmer. Muric smiled, the villagers often did thi.

Turning to him and expecting that that he would have some special insight offered by Aurtus, but the truth was Muric was a learned man, his knowledge coming from books and teachers.

“Sometimes things fall from the heavens, like when a tree falls in the forest, there is no special meaning other than it was the time for that tree to fall, I am sure when they find it, it will be a large rock that is all” he stated and the men nodded.

Except Korl who eyed the young Messenger for a moment and, without speaking, spit the Greenleaf he had packed in his gums, something a lot of farmers did.

Muric eyed the old man as he turned and walked away without saying another word, watching as the farmer headed towards the feast. “How do you know it’s a rock Messenger?” the question bringing Nero from his musings and with a smile he put a reassuring hand on the farmers shoulder “Because it happens my friend, things fall, sometimes from as high as the heavens, mostly simple rocks, it is not a sign from the gods, simply an event that shows all things come to an end” Muric stated excusing himself a he spied familiar face waiting by the door and from the look of the woman she had been crying.

Moving towards he, he smiled “Hello Mar” he said gently, Mar Trisken was a regular attendee who lived with her husband and two children on the outskirts of the village but from the look of her she had been crying Muric observed.

His jaw tightened as he approached the grieving woman.

Had her husband hit her he wondered; Nero had on more than one occasion had to intercede when a husband drunk on wine had taken liberties with his wife.

Women were to be celebrated as the mother, not beaten like a slave he thought shaking his head.

“Mar, what’s wrong my dear” he asked gently as he approached the woman, she was jumpy, glancing around as if at any moment someone would leap out and attack, her red hair hung over half her face, one blue eye shown like a beacon, full of fright and doubt, Nero’s heart went out to her.

“Can we go in Messenger Nero” she asked, her tone pleading and urgent, her eyes continuing to dart around, she was petrified he thought. “Of course,” he said gently leading the poor woman into the keep.

Once she entered Mar continued to walk until she came to the Messengers chambers, the place where he had counseled many in the town, opening the simple wooden door Nero stepped aside allowing her entry first into the small chambers.

The room was a simple one with a desk and three chairs on one side, a wooden divider separated the ‘office’ from the bed and dresser where he slept. Looking around the tiny office, one would find very little of a personal nature.

Nero did not keep trinkets or letters, so instead only one plant and a painting of Aurtus on the throne, the painting that every Keep had in the office and exhibited.

Mar walked over to the stain glass window and stood looking out over the cemetery that resided next to the keep, it had been there since the Keep had been built, the place where those without farmsteads were buried, not quite a paupers cemetery but not too many steps removed.

“Mar, what’s wrong?” Nero asked, walking to the simple desk and to the small appliance that sat there, turning a screw he waited as the two crystals came together and began to heat the water, after a few moments the first bubbles began to rise from the bottom of the small pot.

Turning it off Nero busied himself pouring tea as he collected his thoughts, he needed to get her to open up, she was frightened and closed off, something had happened he thought looking over at Mar and studying her stance and demeanor, she looked on edge and tense.

She turned from the cemetery and regarded the room “Messengers live a simple life committing their time to the congregation instead of hobbies like painting or gardening,” Nero stated apologetically.

Mar looked at him and smiled a weak smile “I understand Messenger,” she simply answered.

He set one of the metal cups down in front of Mar who had come over from the window and sat at the table, She still had fresh tears streaming down her face but she seemed better in control of herself then she had been only a few moments before.

“Tell me,” Nero prodded gently as he sat down, leaning forward to listen to her problem. She sat there for a moment.

Her head hanging, the auburn hair that had once been bright and fiery now looked dulled with the coming of middle age.

Nero sat there waiting patiently, sometimes it took a while for his people to gain courage enough to speak the words that he assumed were coming.

But when she spoke it was not at all what he thought it would be. “My daughter is missing Messenger. The Empress’s soldiers came in the night and took her, stating the need for new servants at the castle.

We tried to stop them, but they almost killed my husband, he is home with a sword wound in his side” she finished.

Her blue eyes locked on his dark brown ones and he felt the electricity, the anger and the resentment from this woman. She was grieving but under that was a deep anger.

“Are you sure it was the Empress’s troops?” he asked. There had been reports, even rumors that children had gone missing and some of them had even cited the Empress’s soldiers as the culprits.

Nero had assumed they were mistaken, why would the Empress be stealing children he wondered.

The Messenger sat back and regarded her, she was not a woman prone to hysteria in fact Nero had never met anyone stronger, if She said it was the Empress’s soldiers then that is what she saw.

The pain she must be going through he thought, having her child taken like that. “Which daughter?” he asked knowing the couple had three.

She lowered her head as if saying her name was painful. “Meery, Messenger. They took my Meery,” she finished as fresh tears began to stream down her cheeks, Nero gently reached over the table and put a hand on her shoulder.

“We will get her back Mar” he said locking eyes with the woman putting as much resolve into his eyes and words.

That didn’t make sense he thought if they wanted new servants for the castle then the older girls would have been the ones they would have taken, Meery was only five, why would they take… his thoughts trailed off as he remembered Meery was the one that had displayed the gift, in fact she was set to leave for Dragon’s keep in two weeks to start training.

Something about that sparked a thought and not a good one, keeping it to himself he kept the worry off his face, it would not be the first-time people had tried to gather those with power for their own ends he thought.

“I will look into this,” Nero said, getting up and coming to stand next to the grieving woman.

His heart went out to her resolving to find out where they had taken her daughter and why. He watched, as Mar, with her head hanging low, walked out into the sunlight.

The day a contrast to the woman’s mood he reflected. Nero did not go back into the keep instead closing the door he walked through the center of town finally coming to the sign that hung above the Crystal Smithy’s.

Nero had no special love for the Mages.

In fact two centuries ago, they had tried to take over the land, claiming those with the gift had been chosen by the gods to lead.

The church along with the emperor had beaten them back, raising and training an army they marched across the land dispatching Mage’s,unfortunately it had not stopped there, the leader of the Messengers deciding that all Mages should be exterminated for the good of the world, that they were a blight on mankind, affront to the gods themselves.

Nero winced as he remember the stories of the first Mage War and the bloody swath the church hat cut through the land in the name of cleansing mankind, finally the mages had been beaten to near extinction, a single band remaining, one led by a man who managed to stop the church in its tracks.

The sides finally came together and signed the Agreement allowing Mages to police themselves and the Order of the Dragon was created, this was the presiding authority on mages, it was also ruled that mages, once discovered would bear the mark of the dragon to identify themselves to all, it was a dark time in their history he thought.

The agreement had stood for nearly a century and a half, if it were true and the Empress was stealing children with the gift, that would be a flagrant breach of the agreement he thought, for a moment his mind wandered as to what that would look like.

If the Agreement were nulled, there would be war, he realized, shivering at the thought of the death and destruction that would follow.

Taking a breath, he cleared his head.

He would have to get to the bottom of this, if not for the grieving mother, then for himself.

Walking into the crystal shop, he spied the short older shop owner standing behind the counter his ample belly resting on the top as he concentrated working on some contraption or another, a pair of round spectacles sat balanced on the edge of his nose as the bright brown eyes concentrated on the small item he held in large hands, hands meant for a laborer, not an engineer Nero thought randomly.

He could never understand how most of the infernal machines worked, though like most he used many, mages still held a level of suspicion for the church, as the old shopkeepers’ eyes rose to greet the messenger, he could see that same suspicion echoed there.

“Hail Kolrim” Nero called making his way forward as he navigated the narrow aisle and making his way towards counter.

The Mage looked up, his dragon tattoo on his cheek prominently showing as he smiled at the Messenger. “Coming to convert me to your holy ways Messenger” Kolrim teased as Nero smiled “Not today mage, not today” he stated.

As Nero watched Kolrim made a motion with his hand and a small tool rose from the box across the counter and floated to him, plucking it from the air he gently pushed the tool into the mechanism he held, repairing the contraption which Nero did not recognize.

“This isn’t a social call; I have a few questions and they are of a dire nature” Nero said.

The smile that had begun to bloom falling away from his face, Kolrim looked up to regard the other man and after a moment of studying his eyes, he put down the tool and nodded to the Messenger.

The two had never been friends but they had shared a mutual respect both knowing the other’s importance to the town, both men loving the town and the people if not the Lord who ran it.

“What’s wrong?” he asked his tone serious, Nero stepped up to the counter, looking around the cluttered shop he ensured they were alone.

“I received a visit from Mar this morning, Meery was taken last night by the Empress’s soldiers, they stated new servants were needed for the castle” he said and watched as the man’s eyes went wide and then distant for a moment.

” That doesn’t make sense, she has older girls that would have made much better choices, besides Meery was set to go to Dragon’s keep in a few weeks, a letter had been dispatched to the capital as is required” he said.

“The crown wouldn’t interfere with that, it is part of the Agreement” he finished and left the next part unsaid but both knew it, doing it knowingly would be a breach of the Agreement, it would mean war.

Then narrowing his eyes, he went into the back as Nero waited, he felt a sense of relief that Kolrim had understood the meaning and that it seemed to scare and bother him as much as it had himself.

Kolrim returned carrying a handful of rolled parchment, dropping them on the counter, he opened one and began to scan it, not finding what he was looking for he grabbed another.

He did this a few more times as Nero waited patiently.

“This is not the first we have heard of this my friend, apparently this has been happening for the past few months as potential initiates have gone missing” he finished his eyes catching Nero’s.

The Messenger could see the haunted look in them, both men understood the weight of the Mages words, this was something that had to be investigated, had to be answered to not do that would invite parties to begin interpreting the actions of the other and that would not be acceptable, that could start a war.

“We have sent representatives to the capital, but they have been turned away, not being allowed to see the Empress” he stated, and Nero nodded understanding now the gravity of the situation, the crown knew what was happening.

If the crown was gathering those that the Mages had indicated were set for training, then the Empress had willingly broken the agreement, worse than that she had done so without warning or notifying the church the crown’s implied ally in forging the Agreement.

Nero felt a pang of fear, he had read the history knew the devastation that the war had brought, if the Empress was now breaking the agreement, there was a potential to tear this land apart, they had to get to the bottom of this, if only to stave off a potential war between the church, the crown and the Mages.

“How can we be sure it was the Empress’s soldiers, is it possible they were just wearing the garb?” Nero asked hopefully.

Kolrim thought about this for a moment as both men stood there the weight of history settling upon their shoulders, the implications of this one action running through the inevitable conclusions in their mind.

“There may be a way” Kolrim said and returned to the back room of the small shop. “It’s something I have been working on, but it’s not quite ready for production” Nero heard the man’s muffled voice through the door of the storage room.

He returned a moment later with a large wooden box, it looked almost amateur in its construction, on one end was a crystal protruding from it, Nero stared at the device suspiciously and then rose to meet the other man’s eyes.

“This might help us,” Kolrim said defensively after seeing the look the Messenger was giving both him and the device Nero sighed shrugging his shoulders in defeat, he didn’t have a better idea so why not he thought shaking his head “at this point I guess I will try anything alright what does it do?” he asked.

A short time later the two men stood outside the small farm where Mar and her family lived, both men bundled against the cold wind that came drifting from the east, the sun hid behind clouds cooling the day further.

Nero surveyed the immediate area as if he could see any evidence that troops had been here, I am no tracker nor would I even begin to know what to look for he thought giving up on the search and coming to stand next to Kolrim as he played with the odd-looking box device, his mass of grey hair blowing in his face and causing him to push it away before continuing to adjust something within the shoddily constructed container.

“What are we doing here Mage, what is this special box of yours?” Nero asked annoyed as the other man continued to rummage around in the makeshift contraption.

After a few moments he began to turn the box eyeing the position and then turning it again, eyeing the position he adjusted it slightly, finally he nodded with approval and reaching inside, turned to regard the Messenger a proud smile as he prepared the device.

“As you know crystals emit an energy, a constant flow of low level power, think of it like a pond, when you throw a stone it disturbs the surface of the water, well every mage has an effect on the power around it and I have spent ten years perfecting how to see that disturbance” he said looking at Nero.

Standing there, the Messenger eyed the other man suspiciously. He was not an expert on the crystals or even magic, but he knew enough to question this man’s description.

“What does that mean?” Nero asked the annoyance and doubt putting an edge to his words and as he watched the other man’s face fell a little sensing his feelings.

“Let me show you” Kolrim breathed excitedly and then with a theatrical flourish flipped a final switch, at first nothing happened as both men stood there quietly eyeing the box, Kolrim cocked his head and reset the switch once more.

Nero waited impatiently as the mage tried a few more adjustments and then with a smile he slammed his hand on top of the wooden box which immediately began to hum and vibrate.

For a moment nothing else happened and then to Nero’s amazement purple tendrils of power snaked out of the box and began to dance over the ground, reaching out to lightly touch upon the buildings and fence of the small farm.

The vines of energy moved forward, caressing the ground and buildings, as they found crystals, they would attach themselves, seeming to draw energy from them.

Nero had never seen anything like this, and his mouth stood agape as the box finished its task, he was not quite sure what it was doing but the visual effect was breathtaking, stepping out of the way as a tendril came close to his foot.

The purple energy returned to the box, this time moving with a purpose as they retreated almost at once and then the humming subsided, the contraption going silent as both men stood there for a moment looking at it.

Kolrim squatted down with a grunt, using his ample belly as a makeshift table he laid tools out and began to gently work inside the box cursing and cooing at the machine.

With a triumphant whoop he flipped a second switch and Nero watched with interest as the crystal that hung out of the end of the box began to glow with that same purple energy.

He stared in amazement as blue and green lights began to join the purple in a kind of spotlight, in the wake of that light, he watched as figures began to resolve, glowing outlines of people standing in place by the door to the farm, after a few minutes the still figures started to move.

The effect was surreal as the blue and purple phantoms played out some scene right before their eyes.

Both men approached the phantoms, doing their best to stay out of way of the crystal as they looked the phantoms over.

“This is amazing” Nero breathed, looking at the simulacrum of a soldier standing at the door.

“Are these the soldiers? how did you do that?” Nero’s questions came out in a steady stream with no pause for the mage to answer and Kolrim shook his head.

“Bottom line, the box views the disruption or changes in energy, all men and women are descended from those who had the ability to manipulate the crystal’s energy, everyone still holds a small piece of that in them, so when the energy is disrupted, that echo is kept for a short period of time, the machine allows us to see the disruption, what you are seeing is the translation of that disruption” he finished.

Nero nodded, he could follow the basics, though still he could not imagine how it was possible, but then again, the impossible and the improbable were the realm of the mage.

“I can’t see the sigil on the tunic” he said squinting at the purple phantom as he tried to see the emblem the soldier wore.

Kolrim cursed and began to tinker in the box again and after a moment it began to clear, and he could see the symbol of a lioness outlined on the soldier’s chest.

“They are the Empress’s solders, or at least wearing their tunic’s Nero said”. Kolrim came to stand next to him and then spied the shield.

“Look at the shield, it’s a protector shield and it’s been well used, also look at the way the soldiers stand, they have been trained this isn’t a costume, these are soldiers Nero, I would put gold on this being soldiers for the Empress” he stated.

After a few moments the wooden box began to vibrate harder and the specter of the soldier began to dim and fade.

“Oh, no,” Kolrim breathed jumping over to the box, but he was too late as black smoke began to belch from within the contraption and the vision of the soldier vanished.

“I take it that’s not good” Nero stated and Kolrim shot him an annoyed look. “It will take me years to build this again” he said defeated. “It was useful Kolrim, it helped, so I imagine for our purposes, it was worth that cost” The Messenger stated and despite the withering looked Kolrim gave him the mage grudgingly nodded in agreement.

The walk back to the town was silent as the two men thought on what they had discovered, Nero knew the discovery would not bode well.

If the Empress truly was stealing those marked for the Order, the Agreement was in peril for the first time in a century, it would mean all-out war between the mages and the crown.

Once back in the small town Kolrim returned to the shop to store his machine and then a few minutes later, joined the Messenger within the keep.

Nero heard the man enter and the main doors close behind him, he called to him to wait as he continued to search storage areas as he carefully went through the large stack of rolled parchment that was stacked on a shelf along one wall.

The Church sent updates regarding information that the Messengers should have, they arrived without fail once a week brought by crow.

Nero read these and then stored them upon the shelf, unfortunately he was no bookkeeper, so they were not in any order, he scanned through the weekly reports and updates from towns and cities trying to ascertain something he had seen.

Every messenger received the updates allowing the parishes to keep informed of the goings-on of the Territory.

He spent close to an hour oblivious to everything around him as he read report after report looking for the thing that had sparked recognition after seeing the events at the farm.

After going through half of them he walked back out to the impatient Kolrim as the man leaned on a pew eyeing the Messenger with an annoyed look on his face.

“There are four reports of this exact same thing Kolrim, according to these, the same thing happens, soldiers show up and take children that are marked for the Order, this cannot stand” he finished looking up at the now shocked Kolrim.

“I knew of a couple, we thought they were merely clerical errors, no one wanted to be the one to accuse the crown of breaking the Agreement Nero” Kolrim whispered, his shoulders slumping as the realization hit him.

The two men sat there for a moment trying to comprehend the possibilities of what a war would mean for their organizations, after a while Nero rose looking to the large mural of Aurtus as if to draw strength or inspiration.

“We need to contact the church and the order, we need to inform them of what we have found, if we are to avert a war, they will need to know” Nero said, Kolrim thought on this and looked about to protest, but them nodded though his eyes looked as if he were resistant to the idea.

Nero looked to him curiously “What’s wrong Kolrim, if you have something to say, say it” he said, and the Mage looked up the fierce intensity in his eyes almost had Nero taking a step back, but he held his ground.

“Think about it, Messenger. The children were all going to the Order, not all of them would have had the papers on file quite yet. Paperwork has a way of being slow” he began.

Nero wasn’t following “What are you getting at Mage?” he asked and for a moment it looked as if Kolrim wasn’t going to answer but then he let out a long-drawn-out sigh, as if Nero was forcing him to state something distasteful and continued.

“I mean that in order for the crown to know which children were going to the order, they would need someone on the inside telling them,” he finished the words seeming to almost hurt him to say.

It took only a moment for Nero to comprehend what Kolrim meant, it was as if someone punched him in the gut. If that was the case then this was not just the crown breaking the Agreement, but this was a conspiracy between the Churches old enemy and its ally.

“We need to warn them regardless, but then we need to find out what happening, I have a sneaking suspicion that we are missing too many facts” he stated.

Motioning for Kolrim to join him they walked to the stables, The young boy who ran the stalls smiled as Nero entered. “I need a letter dispatched to the central keep in Turen, where is your brother toby?” he asked the boy, with a smile he nodded and took off into the small house that sat next to the stalls returning a moment later a gawky young man in tow.

Nero clapped the young man on the back “Klip, are you okay to ride to Turen, I need this letter delivered immediately” he said Klip nodding, taking the letter and the two coins the Messenger Proffered.

“Of course, Messenger, I will leave at once” he said. “Before you go boy, take this to the central building there in Turen as well, deliver it to Master Mage Postin, no one else” Kolrim stated, and the young man nodded solemnly taking another two coins and another letter.

The young man rode out within the hour, the two men watching him as he passed between the gates “Why do I have a sneaking suspicion that we are too late Kolrim, that the events that have transpired are part of a larger machine and we are only now seeing it as it comes to life” Nero said his tone grave as Kolrim turned to regard him, after a moment of contemplation he spoke “Because, I believe you are right Messenger, and if you are I truly hope that Aurtus is looking out for us”.

Kolrim turned and shambled back to his shop

Leaving Nero to look out after the young man as he rode fast across the field and disappeared over the hill and towards Turen.

Nero hoped by contacting the church outside of Vicor anyone who might be in the crown’s pocket would not hear of his warning.

Nero returned to the keep it was next to impossible to keep his mind on the mundane activities that filled his time and the next four days went by agonizingly slow as he awaited a response.

The boy returned the morning of the fifth day and Nero woke to a pounding at the front door. Gathering himself he opened it to see the road weary teen as he held out the sealed letter for the Messenger.

Nero took it, giving the boy another silverling and then closed the door, rushing to his room he tore open the letter began to read.

His heart fell as he read the words and then re-read them. Getting dressed he crossed the town and came to Kolrim’s shop, after a few moments the other man opened the door.

He looked disheveled as if he had not gotten much sleep the night before and, in a sleep, slurred tone asked, “What is it?” upon seeing the look of utter defeat on the face of the Messenger he quickly came awake, motioning Nero to come in and closing the door behind him.

“The central keep wrote back, the Lord Reagent says he will look into it, but for me to stay out of it and continue my duties here” he said, and he could see Kolrim’s shoulders fall.

“Dragon’s keep said the same, sounds like whatever is happening, we are out of the loop” he said defeated. They stood there for a moment not knowing what to do. Finally, Nero shook his head, “We cannot leave this poor girl to her fate Mage, this is our town, our people, it is ours to make right.” Nero said and he could see the slow nod from the Mage as he too came to the same conclusion.

“Do you know anyone who can track those soldiers?” Nero asked and could see Kolrim’s face light up in a smile as he nodded. “I’m with you” he said, and the two men agreed without saying another word, both knew they were going against the wishes of their perspective orders to save a little girl, but neither could leave someone so young and someone they knew to an unknown fate such as this.

Two hours later Nero stood out front of the Keep giving orders to the housekeeper as he spied Kolrim wandering down the street with an older man in hunting leathers.

His grizzled face looked as if it had seem some action Nero thought seeing the scars that adorned his cheeks disappearing under the rats nest of grey beard covering most of his face, however it was the old hunters eyes that drew him, they were active and intelligent as they scanned the area with slow deliberation.

“Muric Nero, this is Jorun, he is an old hunter and retired warden, he will help us find the girl” Kolrim said introducing the two. Nero nodded and put down his pack next to the two others laying on the ground.

Nero had changed from his simple Messenger frock into woodsman leathers, purchased not a day ago from the general store. Looking at the two other men he could see the store clerk had steered him right. “I will take the lead, if I tell you to do something do it” The old man groused and both Kolrim and Nero nodded. After some small talk the three gathered their packs and headed out of the town “Where do we start?” Nero asked excitedly eliciting an annoyed look by the old hunter. “Next town, we go to the tavern, soldiers like to drink Messenger, if they passed through there, then that is where we will find information” he finished.

The three leaving the safety of their Village, turning Nero had a sneaking suspicion he might not see his home again and closing his eyes said a small prayer.
